title: Additivity of the symplectic form in its right argument
statement: Fix a prime $p$ and a natural number $n$, and let $V = \bbf_p^n \times \bbf_p^n$, where $\bbf_p = \bbz/p\bbz$. Equip $V$ with the symplectic form $\omega(u,v) = \sum_{i=0}^{n-1}(x_i z'_i - z_i x'_i)$ for $u = (x,z)$ and $v = (x',z')$. Then $\omega$ is additive in its second argument: for all $x, y, z \in V$, \[ \omega(x,\, y + z) = \omega(x,y) + \omega(x,z). \]
hypotheses_covered: x, y, z range over V = F_p^n × F_p^n
replaced:
Let $p$ be prime and work over the space $V = \bbf_p^n \times \bbf_p^n$ equipped with
the symplectic form $\omega(u,v) = \sum_{i=0}^{n-1}(x_i z'_i - z_i x'_i)$, where $u =
(x,z)$ and $v = (x',z')$. Then for all $x, y, z \in V$,
\[
\omega(x + y, z) = \omega(x, z) + \omega(y, z).
\]
